[engine] A launch configuration must be read by DUMPING it under the configuration you care about, not inferred from the default. Capture the resolved env as a normalised fingerprint so that 'the launch environment did not change' becomes a checkable claim -- and normalise correctly, or the instrument reports noise as change.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-mh-0013 | class: measurement-hygiene | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

run_server.sh's CGC_LOOP_GUARD push sat inside the else-branch of the CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1 test (a missing `fi`), so setting CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1 -- exactly what the comment 6 lines above recommends ('opt back in with CGC_SOFT_POOL_L0=48 CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1=48') -- silently dropped CGC_LOOP_GUARD from the env handed to the server, and CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1 could not restore it because 'push the guard' lived in the branch that only runs when L1 is UNSET. Measured with CGC_DUMP_ENV=1 across four inputs: default -> pushed, L0=48 -> pushed, L1=48 -> DROPPED, L0=48 L1=48 -> DROPPED, plus L1=48 CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1 -> still DROPPED (the earlier 'L0+L1 keeps it' reading was a zsh quoting artifact of my own probe, not a property of the script). No default profile sets L1, so reading the default would never have exposed it. The fingerprint then carried the argument: the normalised dump md5 for prefill250 stabilised at e68a5dc537d626622a9af6c9c7ddf665 once the two volatile line classes were removed, and was IDENTICAL before and after the fix -- which justifies 'this change cannot move the gate numbers' without re-running the gate to find out. Raw (un-normalised) md5 is not stable: prefill250 differed on consecutive runs (8726fb39 vs f898bc94) while prod25 happened to match itself, i.e. a naive fingerprint is wrong in both directions.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

The dump's own volatility: `CGCENV LOG .../llama_server_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log` carries a timestamp, and the `[preflight] free=NN%` / `[guard] ... free=NN%` lines track memory pressure. Without filtering both classes, 'stable' and 'changed' are both unreliable verdicts -- and unfiltered, two profiles in the SAME run set disagreed about which one was stable.
